title: rework-ci-checkpoints-add-dep-deduper-and-toolchain-sync
author: Ethan Liu
description:
Motivation: Our presubmit lane has grown noisy and slow partly due to redundant dependency installations across packages and monorepo-wide lint/test stages that run regardless of surface-area changes. This PR introduces two complementary changes: 1) a lightweight presubmit shim + staged CI checkpoints to provide fast feedback for small changes and staged deeper checks for broader changes, and 2) a dependency deduplication helper and toolchain sync to reduce install time and avoid subtle transitive-version skews.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces .github/workflows/ci-checkpoints.yml which splits CI into three checkpoints: quick (fast lint/typecheck/unit smoke), moderate (integration tests, cross-package contract checks), and full (release smoke and long-running e2e). Checkpoints are annotated so downstream tooling can reroute failure signals.
- Adds scripts/presubmit-shim.sh and a Node-based presubmit manifest that detects touched packages and runs the minimal quick checkpoint locally and in CI. The shim is intentionally tiny (POSIX shell + small Node probe) to keep developer flow fast.
- Adds tools/dep-deduper.py (small Python utility) and scripts/run-dep-dedupe which: 1) analyze lockfiles across packages, 2) propose package.json overrides or shared resolutions, and 3) optionally emit a curated resolutions block for pnpm/yarn that can be reviewed. This reduces duplicated installs and tokenizes mismatched semver windows we saw during a recent incident (SUP-842).
- Introduces infra/toolchain-sync.md and a dev-tools tool that ensures .nvmrc/.python-version/rust-toolchain are consistent across workspace CI images and devcontainers; updates to Dockerfile.dev and devcontainer.json to read the canonical toolchain manifest.
- Small release automation changes: release/rename-artifacts.go makes artifact names deterministic (model: repo-commit-tag) and adds an idempotent check so the release step is resilient when CI retries.

Checklist:
- [x] Introduce ci checkpoints workflow and local shim
- [x] Add dep-deduper and baseline resolutions suggestion
- [x] Sync toolchain manifest for CI and devcontainers
- [x] Update release naming to deterministic artifacts
- [x] Add unit tests for presubmit-shim where applicable
- [x] Documentation: infra/toolchain-sync.md and docs/ci/checkpoints.md

High-level files changed (representative):
- .github/workflows/ci-checkpoints.yml
- scripts/presubmit-shim.sh
- tools/dep-deduper.py
- scripts/run-dep-dedupe (wrapper)
- infra/toolchain-sync.md
- devcontainer.json (toolchain reference)
- Dockerfile.dev (pin node/python versions)
- release/rename-artifacts.go
- package.json (root): small devDependencies sync
- docs/ci/checkpoints.md

Testing and rollout plan:
1) Deploy ci-checkpoints to the repo in staged mode (quick checkpoint enforced on all PRs; moderate/full gated behind label or large-surface change detection).
2) Run dep-deduper against the monorepo lockfiles and open a follow-up chore to apply curated resolutions (this PR emits the report and a suggested resolutions.json).
3) Monitor CI job durations and cache hit rates for two weeks; revert the staged gating if we see unexpected regression.

Backward compatibility: All changes are opt-in for release automation (artifact naming is additive and existing release runner still accepts legacy names for 30 days). The presubmit shim is non-blocking by default and enabled in the CI config immediately to provide faster feedback.

Notes: The dep-deduper intentionally does not auto-apply fixes to package.json; it outputs a small suggestions.json to be reviewed — this reduces risk of sweeping automated changes that could break subtle compatibility constraints.

Related: ENG-2145 (CI fast feedback), ENG-2201 (dep hygiene), SUP-842 (incident: transitive mismatch slowed CI installs).

release_notes: Introduce staged CI checkpoints (quick/moderate/full) and add a dep-deduper tool to analyze and propose lockfile resolutions; include deterministic release artifact naming. Improves presubmit feedback speed and reduces install duplication across the monorepo.
notes_for_owners: Follow-up chore suggested: apply vetted suggestions.json generated by dep-deduper in a separate PR; consider enabling the full checkpoint for selected teams initially. Monitor CI durations and cache hit metrics for 2 weeks.
